title: SPI overview: choose topology and device timing
summary: Select a single target, independent chip selects, a supported daisy chain, or an engineered off-board link.
applies_to: Conventional single-data-rate SPI with device-defined timing and pin behavior.
required_inputs: Devices, topology, SCK mode/rate and edge times
Chip-select timing, target output behavior and power states
verification: Compare both ends' setup/hold, data-valid and enable/disable timing.
limitations: QSPI, OSPI, DDR and memory-mapped flash require separate device-specific channel guidance.

title: SPI single-target routing pattern
summary: Route controller clock, data and select to the target, and target data back to the controller. Budget the return-data timing path.
applies_to: Conventional single-data-rate SPI with device-defined timing and pin behavior.
required_inputs: SCK mode, device delays, board delays and timing margin
Driver edges, loading and reference layers
verification: Check setup/hold at both receiving ends and inspect SCK for extra crossings.
limitations: No universal trace length, equal-length rule or series resistor value applies.

citations.locator: Timing specifications, additional considerations and topologies (standalone, daisy-chain and parallel)

pattern.diagram:
C.SCK  ---> T.SCK
C.MOSI ---> T.SDI
C.CS   ---> T.CS
C.MISO <--- T.SDO
placement: Keep the target near the controller; optional damping belongs near each signal's driver.
routing: Review SCK-to-target plus target-data-to-controller delay for MISO timing.
return_path: Apply the linked plane-continuity and layer-transition guidance.
pitfalls: Slowing the clock does not necessarily remove ringing caused by fast edges.

title: SPI shared bus with independent chip selects
summary: Share clock and data only when inactive targets release MISO. Give each target its own chip-select control.
applies_to: Conventional single-data-rate SPI with device-defined timing and pin behavior.
required_inputs: MISO disable timing and boot states for every target
Fanout, branch geometry, clock mode and loading
verification: Check contention during selection changes and timing at every target.
limitations: Choose trunk, branches or buffering from timing and signal-integrity evidence, not a universal topology rule.

pattern.diagram:
C.SCK/MOSI ---> shared nets ---> T1, T2
C.CS1 ----------------------> T1.CS
C.CS2 ----------------------> T2.CS
C.MISO <--- T1.SDO / T2.SDO (only selected output drives)
placement: Group targets so the shared clock does not acquire long branches.
routing: Evaluate branch reflections and total capacitance; avoid extended test stubs.
return_path: Keep the shared reference continuous beneath all branches.
pitfalls: Some SDO/RDY functions or startup modes do not release the output as assumed.

title: SPI supported serial daisy-chain pattern
summary: Connect target data outputs into subsequent inputs only when every device explicitly supports compatible daisy-chain operation.
applies_to: Conventional single-data-rate SPI with device-defined timing and pin behavior.
required_inputs: Chain support, ordering, frame lengths and timing for each device
verification: Validate complete-chain transfers and setup/hold between adjacent devices.
limitations: Sharing chip selects alone does not create a supported chain.

pattern.diagram:
C.MOSI -> T1.SDI; T1.SDO -> T2.SDI; T2.SDO -> C.MISO
C.SCK -> T1.SCK, T2.SCK
C.CS  -> T1.CS,  T2.CS
placement: Place devices in their selected serial data order.
routing: Keep inter-device data direct while checking shared-clock skew.
return_path: Maintain the common reference for clock and serial data paths.
pitfalls: Do not confuse this logical chain with a shared-MISO bus.

title: SPI off-board link review pattern
summary: Review cable delay, loading, returns and protection before extending SPI off-board; consider dedicated link hardware when necessary.
applies_to: Conventional single-data-rate SPI with device-defined timing and pin behavior.
required_inputs: Cable construction, length, connectors and timing budget
Ground relationship, protection and any translator/isolator delays
verification: Check waveforms and timing across the complete link in both directions.
limitations: There is no universal maximum SPI cable length. The pattern does not select a cable or link technology.

pattern.diagram:
Controller <-> optional link hardware <-> connector/cable <-> Target
SCK/MOSI/CS forward; MISO reverse; returns planned with the cable
placement: Keep connector-boundary protection and any link hardware on the intended signal path.
routing: Include forward clock and reverse data propagation in the timing analysis.
return_path: Assign nearby cable returns rather than treating the ground pin as sufficient evidence.
pitfalls: A lower SCK frequency cannot repair an overvoltage or an unsuitable return path.
